experiments.summary: rank-one, ray, relative determinant, gamma real > 0, gauge, Ward, approximate bound on 200 random complex instances with non-unitary D
forced H(x)=1: kernel dimension 1 and Re(conj(Hz)<g,Dz>) = gamma|Hz|^2
bilinear pairing breaks Ward; D* in place of D^-1 breaks the ray
2x2 crossing satisfies every M74 identity yet A(s) has a negative eigenvalue for s > 0: the secular algebra alone cannot exclude a crossing
min/max of pi^2 e/|z|^2 beyond -1/+1; control without zero sum gives e = 0
telescoped mass exact; optimal constant decreasing to 1/4 (signal); 1/4 + 0.01 fails at K = 80
entry derivative <= 2 + 4 pi K; window inside (0,1) and below -|z|^2/(2 pi^2); true negative run >= ~198 x 2 eta (eta is crude)

actual canonical float matrices, K = 2..5, L = 0.25..6: rank-one relation B D - D A = g H holds to 2e-15 (consistent with the Lean theorem); on the 46 float-resolved (K, L) points B > 0, A > 0 and the secular margin 1 - T(L) > 0 (min 4.4e-4 at K = 3, L = 2.75), with det A / det B = 1 - T to 3e-9; the pole and prime channel contributions to T cancel to relative size up to 7e9
experiments.caveat: 50 grid points are below float64 resolution (lambda_min < 1e-10 x matrix scale) and are reported as unresolved, not as signs; no certified enclosure
